newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end 0.8 pct down on U.S. weakness.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end 0.8 pct down on U.S. weakness.

text.p: The Australian share market ended 0.8 percent lower on Monday in reaction to U.S. weakness on Friday, but turnover was meagre as a bank holiday in New South Wales sidelined many investors.
"There was not much happening today, because we just didn't have the weight of money, with it being a bank holiday here," said one Sydney-based dealer.
The All Ordinaries index closed 21.5 points down at 2,706.0 in turnover of only A$421 million (US$312 million), about half the normal total.
Banking shares suffered the most as sharply higher bond yields, triggered by a weak U.S. bond market, took its toll on the sector and pulled the index 1.1 percent lower.
Among the major banks, ANZ ended 19 cents lower at A$10.51 and National Australia 14 cents down at A$19.37. Westpac lost 16 cents or almost 1.9 percent to close at A$8.46.

The big resources stocks ended mixed. BHP closed 16 cents lower at A$17.85, while Rio Tinto lost 12.3 cents to A$20.67. Gold and nickel producer WMC rebounded from early losses to end six cents firmer at A$7.70.
Dealers said there was no news behind WMC's gains, but that the stock had been come down to attractive levels recently.
There were few domestic factors driving the market on Monday but this could change with the many half and full-year company results coming up in the next few weeks, dealers said.
"Maybe we'll get a bit more domestic direction from figures later this week, including labour force data on Thursday, and with the reporting season starting," one dealer said.
Most listings with earnings reports due this week lost ground in line with the overall market.

Soft-drink group Coca-Cola Amatil recovered some early losses, but still ended 11.2 cents down at A$16.138 ahead of Wednesday's first-half profit announcement. The bottler is seen showing a slightly better net profit of about A$60 million for the half year to June 30, up from A$58.9 million a year ago.
"They are coming off a very weak base in the second half of last year," a Sydney-based analyst said.

Agricultural and chemicals group Wesfarmers lost 19 cents to A$12.09 ahead of Tuesday's full-year report, while diversified manufacturer Pacific BBA ended six cents weaker at A$5.64 ahead of its half-year report, also on Tuesday.
The number of declining stocks more than doubled advancing issues, and most of the day's winners had only small turnover.
The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is not expected to make any policy changes at its monthly meeting on Tuesday after last week's interest rate cut to 5.0 percent from 5.5 percent.
